From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. 9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer-side review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Preliminary note on the "Reviewer Efficiency Note":** The Seller's package asserts that clauses marked [STANDARD] have been "cleared by both sides" and that the Buyer has "already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package." That is incorrect – the Seller cannot pre-clear its own positions, and nothing in our instructions records Buyer acceptance. I have reviewed every clause on its merits. Recommend the Buyer's response letter expressly reject the [STANDARD]/[OPEN] framing and record that all points remain open.

**Overall:** The Seller's package is heavily seller-favourable and, on four items (Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses, title), does not even meet the stated baseline of a debt-free/cash-free acquisition of 100% of the shares with Completion certainty. Several points (SPA-N-004, -005, -008, -009, -014, -015) should be treated as deal-critical, not negotiable drafting points.

---

## SPA-N-001: General liability cap (cl 12.1)
- **Seller position:** Aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims capped at 20% of price (AUD 4,800,000).
- **Buyer wants:** Higher general cap – open at 100% of price, settle no lower than 30–50% (AUD 7.2m–12m) – with the cap expressly confined to *general* warranties only; fundamental warranties, tax, and specific indemnities (Ironquay, DD-006, Riverlark) uncapped or capped at full price and sitting outside the 20% pool.
- **Recommendation:** Reject 20% as drafted; counter at 50% and ring-fence indemnities and fundamental/tax warranties from the cap.
  *Reason:* With ~30% of revenue dependent on one counterparty (Bluefen) and multiple unresolved DD issues, a 20% cap is thin and the Seller's drafting would draw everything into it.

## SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket (cl 12.2)
- **Seller position:** De minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; basket is a *deductible* (only excess recoverable).
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis ~AUD 10,000–12,000 (≈0.05% of price); basket ~AUD 120,000–240,000 (0.5–1%) structured as a *tipping* basket (first dollar recoverable once exceeded); related claims aggregated for the de minimis; thresholds not to apply to fundamental warranties, tax, or specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation:** Accept a basket concept but convert to tipping basket, lower de minimis to ~AUD 10,000, aggregate series claims, and carve out indemnities/fundamental/tax.
  *Reason:* A deductible basket on a AUD 24m deal permanently forfeits the first AUD 250k of loss, and a AUD 25k de minimis would exclude a large share of realistic operational claims (e.g. the Sandbar renewals are individually only AUD 110k).

## SPA-N-003: General claims time limit (cl 12.3 / 13)
- **Seller position:** General warranty claims must be notified within 18 months; "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months for general warranties (minimum: long enough to capture one full audit cycle post-Completion); tax warranties/tax indemnity for 7 years (or statutory amendment period plus 6 months); fundamental/title warranties 6–7 years or unlimited; notification period followed by a reasonable period (6–9 months) to commence proceedings; reversal of the default rule so limitations apply *only* where expressly stated.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 24 months general / 7 years tax / 7+ years fundamental, and strike the "applies to all Claims" default.
  *Reason:* 18 months may not cover the first post-Completion audited accounts, and the default-application rule silently extends the short period to tax, title, and indemnity claims.

## SPA-N-004: Fundamental / Title regime
- **Seller position:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same cap (20%), basket, and 18-month limit as general warranties "for administrative simplicity."
- **Buyer wants:** Fundamental warranties (title to shares, capacity, authority, no encumbrances, solvency, share capital) capped at 100% of price (or uncapped), no de minimis/basket, and a 6–7 year (or unlimited) claims period.
- **Recommendation:** Reject outright – this is a walk-away point.
  *Reason:* If title fails, the Buyer has paid AUD 24m for nothing and the Seller would owe at most AUD 4.8m; "administrative simplicity" is not a reason to accept recovering 20 cents in the dollar on the core of the bargain.

## SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller position:** None offered. Cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 apply limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature," and cl 12.3 applies limitations to all Claims by default – i.e. the package as drafted would limit the Seller's liability even for fraud.
- **Buyer wants:** Express carve-out: no limitation (cap, threshold, time limit, exclusive remedy, non-reliance, knowledge qualifier) applies to any Claim arising from fraud, fraudulent misrepresentation, wilful concealment, or wilful default by the Seller, the Company, or their officers/advisers.
- **Recommendation:** Insert a comprehensive fraud/wilful misconduct carve-out as a non-negotiable.
  *Reason:* A clause purporting to limit liability for fraud is likely unenforceable in any event, but its absence signals intent and creates argument – it must be express.

## SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope (Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter §1)
- **Seller position:** General disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012 as at 22 Sept 2026), the Accounts, statutory registers, and "publicly searchable corporate records"; §1.4 disclaims any admission that consents, payments, notices or remediation are required.
- **Buyer wants:** Disclosure only of matters "fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter disclosed"; general data room disclosure deleted or confined to documents specifically indexed against a specific warranty; no disclosure of public registers (or limited to ASIC company search and PPSR of the Company as at a fixed date); no disclosure against fundamental warranties, tax warranties or indemnities; data room frozen (USB/index annexed) to the Disclosure Letter.
- **Recommendation:** Reject general disclosure; require specific disclosure against numbered warranties with a "fair disclosure" standard.
  *Reason:* Wholesale data-room and public-record disclosure effectively empties the warranties of content – every issue the Seller is aware of becomes "disclosed" without the Seller having to identify it.

## SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier (cl 8.3)
- **Seller position:** No claim for any matter of which the Buyer "or its advisers" had knowledge, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records."
- **Buyer wants:** Delete cl 8.3 entirely. Fallback: limited to *actual* knowledge of a small named deal team (not advisers, not constructive/imputed knowledge), and only of matters *fairly disclosed* in the Disclosure Letter; expressly not applying to indemnities or fundamental warranties.
- **Recommendation:** Delete; if pressed, accept named-individuals actual-knowledge only, with no "discoverable" or adviser imputation.
  *Reason:* "Discoverable from the data room or public records" is a constructive-knowledge standard that, combined with general disclosure (SPA-N-006), would defeat virtually every warranty claim.

## SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3; DL §2)
- **Seller position:** "Addressed" by reasonable endeavours; condition treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. Disclosure Letter confirms no final written consent exists and no evidence that cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
- **Buyer wants:** Unconditional written Bluefen consent (and satisfaction/waiver of all cl 11.3 conditions) as a Condition Precedent for the Buyer's benefit only, waivable only by the Buyer; "all reasonable endeavours" or "best endeavours" obligation on the Seller, with the Seller bearing any consent cost; Buyer approval of the form of consent; long-stop date; and a specific indemnity or price-adjustment / escrow if Bluefen terminates or reduces scope within 12 months of Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Convert to a hard CP (consent in agreed form, conditions satisfied) with termination right, plus a post-Completion Bluefen revenue protection (escrow of ~AUD 2.4m or earn-out adjustment).
  *Reason:* Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue; a *conditional* consent that is deemed "satisfied" on delivery of a piece of paper transfers all change-of-control risk to the Buyer.

## SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7; DL §3)
- **Seller position:** AUD ~3.2m facility outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion." Disclosure Letter confirms facility not repaid and no discharge of security included.
- **Buyer wants:** Full repayment and release at or before Completion: executed payout letter and deed of release/discharge of all security (including PPSR discharge) delivered as a Completion deliverable; repayment funded from the purchase price via the funds flow (consistent with debt-free/cash-free); Riverlark cl 8.1 change-of-control consent either obtained or rendered moot by payout; Seller indemnity for any residual amount, break costs, or security not released.
- **Recommendation:** Reject post-Completion release; require repay-and-release at Completion with price deduction and Seller indemnity.
  *Reason:* Under a debt-free/cash-free price the Buyer would otherwise pay AUD 24m and inherit AUD 3.2m of secured debt with an uncured change-of-control default – a ~13% overpayment on day one.

## SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses (DD-005; DL §5)
- **Seller position:** AUD 420,000 of Completion bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow; disclosure silent on payroll tax, superannuation, on-costs.
- **Buyer wants:** Bonuses treated as Transaction Costs / Debt-like item: AUD 420,000 *plus* employer on-costs (superannuation ~12%, payroll tax ~5–6% NSW, i.e. ~AUD 495k–505k grossed up) either paid by the Seller pre-Completion or deducted from the price in the funds flow; Company to pay post-Completion only from funds provided by the Seller; specific indemnity for any shortfall; confirmation of any PAYG withholding obligations and that "continued employment" conditions do not create retention liabilities on the Buyer.
- **Recommendation:** Itemise in funds flow as a price deduction (grossed-up) with Seller indemnity.
  *Reason:* The bonuses are triggered by Completion and payable by the Company, so absent adjustment the Buyer – not the Seller – funds them.

## SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity (cl 11.1; DD-004, DD-010; DL §4)
- **Seller position:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment (AUD 180,000) and "considered adequate." Disclosure confirms the AUD 180k is open per DD-010, no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room, and IP transfer is conditional on cleared payment of *every* SOW3 fee.
- **Buyer wants:** (1) Pre-Completion: Seller to cause payment in full of all SOW3 fees and deliver a confirmatory deed of assignment of all Project Materials IP from Ironquay as a Completion deliverable; (2) specific indemnity covering not just the AUD 180k but all loss from any defect in title to the Project Materials (licence fees, re-development cost, infringement claims, business interruption) – capped at purchase price, not subject to basket/de minimis, 6-year period; (3) IP warranty that Company owns all IP in its products free of third-party claims.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the AUD 180k-only indemnity; require payment + confirmatory assignment at Completion and a broad IP-title indemnity.
  *Reason:* The exposure is loss of ownership of the deliverables (and anything built on them), not the AUD 180k invoice – the Seller's framing caps the remedy at the cheapest number available.

## SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Sch 6; DD-006; DL §6)
- **Seller position:** "Preliminary operational matter," not expected to be material; no admission of breach. Disclosure confirms ~1,240 personal records sent to an unintended external address; unknown whether accessed; investigation incomplete; notification requirement unassessed.
- **Buyer wants:** Seller to complete investigation pre-Completion and deliver a written report (including external privacy counsel's view on OAIC/Notifiable Data Breaches scheme obligations and any contractual notification obligations to the data subjects' employers/clients); confirmation that any required notifications have been made; specific indemnity for all loss arising from the DD-006 incident (regulatory penalties, notification costs, remediation, third-party and customer claims, loss of any customer contract attributable to the incident) – outside cap/basket, 6-year period; privacy/data-security warranties not qualified by the general disclosure; Buyer right to be consulted on any notification before Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Treat as an identified-risk indemnity; do not accept "not expected to be material" from the party that hasn't finished investigating.
  *Reason:* Under the Privacy Act NDB scheme an uncontained disclosure of 1,240 records can be a reportable eligible data breach with civil penalty exposure, and the entity carrying that risk after Completion is the Buyer.

## SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (DD-008, DD-011; DL §8)
- **Seller position:** Three AUD 110,000 renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are "ordinary-course operating costs."
- **Buyer wants:** Clarity on whether these are (a) genuine recurring ordinary-course costs already reflected in the forecast/working capital, or (b) accrued, deferred or non-terminable commitments, or a single AUD 330k arrangement split into three contracts (note they are "related" and must be "read together for timing/scope" – possible threshold-splitting). If committed and unpaid at Completion, treat as Debt-like/accrued liability in the completion accounts; if ordinary course, ensure they sit in normalised working capital; obtain the underlying contracts and termination terms.
- **Recommendation:** Require Seller to confirm status and terms in writing; include in completion-accounts definitions as either accrued liability or working capital; do not accept the "ordinary course" label unexamined.
  *Reason:* Three identical, related renewals each just above the proposed de minimis and together above the basket is a pattern that warrants verification, and AUD 330k is material against a AUD 250k basket.

## SPA-N-014: Category separation (cl 9.3 / 12.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)
- **Seller position:** All limitations, the exclusive-remedy clause and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature," and any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly excluded. Capacity/title also folded in.
- **Buyer wants:** A clear, separately drafted regime for each category: (1) general warranties (cap/basket/18–24m); (2) fundamental warranties (100%/no basket/6–7 yrs+); (3) tax warranties and tax indemnity (100%/no basket/7 yrs); (4) specific indemnities – Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses (100%/no basket/6 yrs, not subject to disclosure or Buyer knowledge); (5) fraud – unlimited; plus Completion obligations (payment of price, delivery of title) wholly outside the limitation regime. Exclusive-remedy and non-reliance confined to warranty claims and not extending to indemnities, Completion obligations, fraud, or statutory rights that cannot be excluded (e.g. ACL s 18 to the extent applicable).
- **Recommendation:** Redraft Sch/cl 12 as a category table; flip the default so limitations apply only where expressly stated.
  *Reason:* The Seller's "all Claims" drafting is the mechanism that collapses every protection into the 20% / 18-month box – fixing this structurally resolves several of the items above at once.

## SPA-N-015: Title verification (DL §10; DD-012)
- **Seller position:** Title evidenced by the Company's own share register at DD-012; disclosure expressly notes the Buyer has not completed its own verification.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent verification before signing: current ASIC company extract (members, share structure, officeholders, charges), PPSR search against the Company *and* Harbourglass for security over shares, review of constitution for pre-emptive rights/transfer restrictions, confirmation no options/convertibles/shareholder agreements, Riverlark security package (does it include a share mortgage or specific security over the shares?). Completion deliverables: original share certificates (or lost-certificate indemnity), executed transfer, board minutes approving transfer and registration, updated register. Unqualified fundamental title warranties (see SPA-N-004) not subject to data-room disclosure.
- **Recommendation:** Run ASIC/PPSR searches and constitution review now, and make title warranties absolute and un-disclosed-against.
  *Reason:* A company's internal register is self-serving evidence; combined with the Seller's attempt to cap title warranties at 20% and disclose "public records" generally, the Buyer currently has no reliable protection for the one thing it is buying.

## SPA-N-016: Tax / IP open terms
- **Seller position:** Tax and IP warranty positions "settled under the general regime" (i.e. 20% cap, AUD 250k basket, 18 months, general disclosure).
- **Buyer wants:** **Tax:** full tax indemnity for all pre-Completion tax (including payroll tax/super on the bonuses, any GST/withholding, and R&D tax incentive clawback risk typical for an analytics business), capped at price, no basket, 7-year period (or amendment period + 6 months), not qualified by disclosure or Buyer knowledge, with tax conduct-of-claims provisions; tax warranties with same profile. **IP:** warranties that the Company solely owns or validly licenses all IP in its products/data, all employee and contractor IP has been assigned (Ironquay is the known gap – likely not the only contractor), no open-source copyleft contamination, no infringement claims; IP warranties either fundamental or in an elevated tier (50–100% cap, 3–6 years); Ironquay-specific indemnity per SPA-N-011.
- **Recommendation:** Treat tax and IP as *not* settled; propose elevated separate tiers and a standalone tax indemnity.
  *Reason:* For an analytics company the IP *is* the asset and tax exposure runs for years after an 18-month window – neither fits the general regime, and the Seller's "settled" is an assertion, not an agreement.

---

## Suggested priority for the Buyer's mark-up letter

| Priority | Items | Nature |
|---|---|---|
| **Deal-critical / CP** | N-008 Bluefen, N-009 Riverlark, N-015 Title, N-004 Fundamental regime, N-005 Fraud | Must be fixed before signing |
| **Price / funds flow** | N-010 Bonuses, N-013 Sandbar (if committed), N-009 payout | Adjust price or funds flow |
| **Specific indemnities** | N-011 Ironquay, N-012 DD-006, N-016 Tax | Outside cap/basket/disclosure |
| **Limitation architecture** | N-014 Category separation, N-001 Cap, N-002 Basket, N-003 Time limits | Redraft as tiered regime |
| **Disclosure architecture** | N-006 Scope, N-007 Knowledge | Specific/fair disclosure only |

Finally, recommend the cover letter state in terms: (i) the Buyer does not accept the [STANDARD]/[OPEN] categorisation or any statement that the limitation or disclosure package has been agreed; (ii) all positions remain subject to contract and completion of due diligence; and (iii) the Seller is requested to supplement the data room with the missing Bluefen consent, Riverlark payout/discharge documents, Ironquay payment receipt and assignment, DD-006 investigation report, and Sandbar contracts before the next turn of the draft.

## SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller position:** None offered. Cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 apply limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature," and cl 12.3 applies limitations to all Claims by default – i.e. the package as drafted would limit the Seller's liability even for fraud.
- **Buyer wants:** Express carve-out: no limitation (cap, threshold, time limit, exclusive remedy, non-reliance, knowledge qualifier) applies to any Claim arising from fraud, fraudulent misrepresentation, wilful concealment, or wilful default by the Seller, the Company, or their officers/advisers.
- **Recommendation:** Insert a comprehensive fraud/wilful misconduct carve-out as a non-negotiable.
  *Reason:* A clause purporting to limit liability for fraud is likely unenforceable in any event, but its absence signals intent and creates argument – it must be express.

## SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope (Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter §1)
- **Seller position:** General disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012 as at 22 Sept 2026), the Accounts, statutory registers, and "publicly searchable corporate records"; §1.4 disclaims any admission that consents, payments, notices or remediation are required.
- **Buyer wants:** Disclosure only of matters "fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter disclosed"; general data room disclosure deleted or confined to documents specifically indexed against a specific warranty; no disclosure of public registers (or limited to ASIC company search and PPSR of the Company as at a fixed date); no disclosure against fundamental warranties, tax warranties or indemnities; data room frozen (USB/index annexed) to the Disclosure Letter.
- **Recommendation:** Reject general disclosure; require specific disclosure against numbered warranties with a "fair disclosure" standard.
  *Reason:* Wholesale data-room and public-record disclosure effectively empties the warranties of content – every issue the Seller is aware of becomes "disclosed" without the Seller having to identify it.

## SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier (cl 8.3)
- **Seller position:** No claim for any matter of which the Buyer "or its advisers" had knowledge, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records."
- **Buyer wants:** Delete cl 8.3 entirely. Fallback: limited to *actual* knowledge of a small named deal team (not advisers, not constructive/imputed knowledge), and only of matters *fairly disclosed* in the Disclosure Letter; expressly not applying to indemnities or fundamental warranties.
- **Recommendation:** Delete; if pressed, accept named-individuals actual-knowledge only, with no "discoverable" or adviser imputation.
  *Reason:* "Discoverable from the data room or public records" is a constructive-knowledge standard that, combined with general disclosure (SPA-N-006), would defeat virtually every warranty claim.

## SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3; DL §2)
- **Seller position:** "Addressed" by reasonable endeavours; condition treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. Disclosure Letter confirms no final written consent exists and no evidence that cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
- **Buyer wants:** Unconditional written Bluefen consent (and satisfaction/waiver of all cl 11.3 conditions) as a Condition Precedent for the Buyer's benefit only, waivable only by the Buyer; "all reasonable endeavours" or "best endeavours" obligation on the Seller, with the Seller bearing any consent cost; Buyer approval of the form of consent; long-stop date; and a specific indemnity or price-adjustment / escrow if Bluefen terminates or reduces scope within 12 months of Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Convert to a hard CP (consent in agreed form, conditions satisfied) with termination right, plus a post-Completion Bluefen revenue protection (escrow of ~AUD 2.4m or earn-out adjustment).
  *Reason:* Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue; a *conditional* consent that is deemed "satisfied" on delivery of a piece of paper transfers all change-of-control risk to the Buyer.

## SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7; DL §3)
- **Seller position:** AUD ~3.2m facility outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion." Disclosure Letter confirms facility not repaid and no discharge of security included.
- **Buyer wants:** Full repayment and release at or before Completion: executed payout letter and deed of release/discharge of all security (including PPSR discharge) delivered as a Completion deliverable; repayment funded from the purchase price via the funds flow (consistent with debt-free/cash-free); Riverlark cl 8.1 change-of-control consent either obtained or rendered moot by payout; Seller indemnity for any residual amount, break costs, or security not released.
- **Recommendation:** Reject post-Completion release; require repay-and-release at Completion with price deduction and Seller indemnity.
  *Reason:* Under a debt-free/cash-free price the Buyer would otherwise pay AUD 24m and inherit AUD 3.2m of secured debt with an uncured change-of-control default – a ~13% overpayment on day one.

## SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses (DD-005; DL §5)
- **Seller position:** AUD 420,000 of Completion bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow; disclosure silent on payroll tax, superannuation, on-costs.
- **Buyer wants:** Bonuses treated as Transaction Costs / Debt-like item: AUD 420,000 *plus* employer on-costs (superannuation ~12%, payroll tax ~5–6% NSW, i.e. ~AUD 495k–505k grossed up) either paid by the Seller pre-Completion or deducted from the price in the funds flow; Company to pay post-Completion only from funds provided by the Seller; specific indemnity for any shortfall; confirmation of any PAYG withholding obligations and that "continued employment" conditions do not create retention liabilities on the Buyer.
- **Recommendation:** Itemise in funds flow as a price deduction (grossed-up) with Seller indemnity.
  *Reason:* The bonuses are triggered by Completion and payable by the Company, so absent adjustment the Buyer – not the Seller – funds them.

## SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity (cl 11.1; DD-004, DD-010; DL §4)
- **Seller position:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment (AUD 180,000) and "considered adequate." Disclosure confirms the AUD 180k is open per DD-010, no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room, and IP transfer is conditional on cleared payment of *every* SOW3 fee.
- **Buyer wants:** (1) Pre-Completion: Seller to cause payment in full of all SOW3 fees and deliver a confirmatory deed of assignment of all Project Materials IP from Ironquay as a Completion deliverable; (2) specific indemnity covering not just the AUD 180k but all loss from any defect in title to the Project Materials (licence fees, re-development cost, infringement claims, business interruption) – capped at purchase price, not subject to basket/de minimis, 6-year period; (3) IP warranty that Company owns all IP in its products free of third-party claims.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the AUD 180k-only indemnity; require payment + confirmatory assignment at Completion and a broad IP-title indemnity.
  *Reason:* The exposure is loss of ownership of the deliverables (and anything built on them), not the AUD 180k invoice – the Seller's framing caps the remedy at the cheapest number available.

## SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Sch 6; DD-006; DL §6)
- **Seller position:** "Preliminary operational matter," not expected to be material; no admission of breach. Disclosure confirms ~1,240 personal records sent to an unintended external address; unknown whether accessed; investigation incomplete; notification requirement unassessed.
- **Buyer wants:** Seller to complete investigation pre-Completion and deliver a written report (including external privacy counsel's view on OAIC/Notifiable Data Breaches scheme obligations and any contractual notification obligations to the data subjects' employers/clients); confirmation that any required notifications have been made; specific indemnity for all loss arising from the DD-006 incident (regulatory penalties, notification costs, remediation, third-party and customer claims, loss of any customer contract attributable to the incident) – outside cap/basket, 6-year period; privacy/data-security warranties not qualified by the general disclosure; Buyer right to be consulted on any notification before Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Treat as an identified-risk indemnity; do not accept "not expected to be material" from the party that hasn't finished investigating.
  *Reason:* Under the Privacy Act NDB scheme an uncontained disclosure of 1,240 records can be a reportable eligible data breach with civil penalty exposure, and the entity carrying that risk after Completion is the Buyer.

## SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (DD-008, DD-011; DL §8)
- **Seller position:** Three AUD 110,000 renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are "ordinary-course operating costs."
- **Buyer wants:** Clarity on whether these are (a) genuine recurring ordinary-course costs already reflected in the forecast/working capital, or (b) accrued, deferred or non-terminable commitments, or a single AUD 330k arrangement split into three contracts (note they are "related" and must be "read together for timing/scope" – possible threshold-splitting). If committed and unpaid at Completion, treat as Debt-like/accrued liability in the completion accounts; if ordinary course, ensure they sit in normalised working capital; obtain the underlying contracts and termination terms.
- **Recommendation:** Require Seller to confirm status and terms in writing; include in completion-accounts definitions as either accrued liability or working capital; do not accept the "ordinary course" label unexamined.
  *Reason:* Three identical, related renewals each just above the proposed de minimis and together above the basket is a pattern that warrants verification, and AUD 330k is material against a AUD 250k basket.

## SPA-N-014: Category separation (cl 9.3 / 12.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)
- **Seller position:** All limitations, the exclusive-remedy clause and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature," and any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly excluded. Capacity/title also folded in.
- **Buyer wants:** A clear, separately drafted regime for each category: (1) general warranties (cap/basket/18–24m); (2) fundamental warranties (100%/no basket/6–7 yrs+); (3) tax warranties and tax indemnity (100%/no basket/7 yrs); (4) specific indemnities – Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses (100%/no basket/6 yrs, not subject to disclosure or Buyer knowledge); (5) fraud – unlimited; plus Completion obligations (payment of price, delivery of title) wholly outside the limitation regime. Exclusive-remedy and non-reliance confined to warranty claims and not extending to indemnities, Completion obligations, fraud, or statutory rights that cannot be excluded (e.g. ACL s 18 to the extent applicable).
- **Recommendation:** Redraft Sch/cl 12 as a category table; flip the default so limitations apply only where expressly stated.
  *Reason:* The Seller's "all Claims" drafting is the mechanism that collapses every protection into the 20% / 18-month box – fixing this structurally resolves several of the items above at once.

## SPA-N-015: Title verification (DL §10; DD-012)
- **Seller position:** Title evidenced by the Company's own share register at DD-012; disclosure expressly notes the Buyer has not completed its own verification.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent verification before signing: current ASIC company extract (members, share structure, officeholders, charges), PPSR search against the Company *and* Harbourglass for security over shares, review of constitution for pre-emptive rights/transfer restrictions, confirmation no options/convertibles/shareholder agreements, Riverlark security package (does it include a share mortgage or specific security over the shares?). Completion deliverables: original share certificates (or lost-certificate indemnity), executed transfer, board minutes approving transfer and registration, updated register. Unqualified fundamental title warranties (see SPA-N-004) not subject to data-room disclosure.
- **Recommendation:** Run ASIC/PPSR searches and constitution review now, and make title warranties absolute and un-disclosed-against.
  *Reason:* A company's internal register is self-serving evidence; combined with the Seller's attempt to cap title warranties at 20% and disclose "public records" generally, the Buyer currently has no reliable protection for the one thing it is buying.

## SPA-N-016: Tax / IP open terms
- **Seller position:** Tax and IP warranty positions "settled under the general regime" (i.e. 20% cap, AUD 250k basket, 18 months, general disclosure).
- **Buyer wants:** **Tax:** full tax indemnity for all pre-Completion tax (including payroll tax/super on the bonuses, any GST/withholding, and R&D tax incentive clawback risk typical for an analytics business), capped at price, no basket, 7-year period (or amendment period + 6 months), not qualified by disclosure or Buyer knowledge, with tax conduct-of-claims provisions; tax warranties with same profile. **IP:** warranties that the Company solely owns or validly licenses all IP in its products/data, all employee and contractor IP has been assigned (Ironquay is the known gap – likely not the only contractor), no open-source copyleft contamination, no infringement claims; IP warranties either fundamental or in an elevated tier (50–100% cap, 3–6 years); Ironquay-specific indemnity per SPA-N-011.
- **Recommendation:** Treat tax and IP as *not* settled; propose elevated separate tiers and a standalone tax indemnity.
  *Reason:* For an analytics company the IP *is* the asset and tax exposure runs for years after an 18-month window – neither fits the general regime, and the Seller's "settled" is an assertion, not an agreement.
